reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the order and refund data myself. A recorded payout can't be undone, so I'll start by listing the orders.
Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds myself, since payouts can't be recalled. I'll check the refund records against the handoff message.
The refund records match the handoff exactly, and each refund maps to an existing order. I'll get the net balance for each customer from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 44848 matches my own check: orders 39605 + 19145 = 58750, minus refund 13902 on order 163 gives 44848. I'll check birch next before recording any payouts.

Birch's net balance of 1461 matches my check: orders 7280 + 4413 = 11693, minus refunds 6723 + 3509 = 10232, leaves 1461. Cobalt has no refunds, so its expected balance is 33787 + 2029 = 35816. I'll confirm that with net_balance before recording any payouts.
All three net balances match my own calculations from the orders and refunds, and the refunds match the handoff. Nothing looks wrong, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme for 44848.
Acme's payout of 44848 was recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 1461 matches my own calculation from the orders and refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's net balance of 35816 matches my own calculation from its two orders with no refunds, so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each amount matched the net_balance figure and my own check from the orders and refunds, so the batch is complete.
